Title: Arrange Pattern with Arrangement Points/Flip Wrap Direction
Content: Objective Arrangement Points are created based on the Bounding Volume surrounding the Avatar, and are arranged on the Avatar according to the Bounding Volume's curves. Note: Precise arrangement is available by using Gizmo or Property Editor even after arranging with Arrangement Points. Location Avatar Display Show Arrangement Points Operation Follow the indicated guideline: Avatar Display Show Arrangement Points The Arrangement Points appear around the Avatar. Select a Pattern and hover the mouse over an Arrangement Point. A preview of the Pattern placement is being displayed (ver2.4.0). Select a desired Arrangement Point. The center of the Pattern is now being placed according to the selected Arrangement Point. Symmetric Arrangement occurs as long as the Patterns and Arrangement Points have symmetry applied (ver3.0.0). Note: Flip Wrap Direction Patterns that the length are longer than the Bounding Volume, such as cuffs, get arranged spiral. Right-click on patterns in the 3D window Click Flip Wrap Direction to flip its direction.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Collision Thickness
Content: Objective Simulation thickness is invisible set property that represents the collision limit for Garments to result smooth Simulation. By default, the Simulation thickness from the Garment Pattern is set 1.5mm on each side, for a total of 3mm, and this value is adjustable as required. Lower the thickness value to work on Garments that are more likely to be form-fitting, or increase the thickness value to use as padding and etc. Note: For the same reason, the default value of Avatar thickness (Skin Offset) is set for 3mm. For form-fitting Garments or accurate fitting measurement, it is recommended that Skin Offset is adjusted alongside the Simulation thickness. Location Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window Property Editor Simulation Properties Add'l Thickness-Collision Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window Property Editor Simulation Properties Add'l Thickness-Collision Enter desired rendering thickness value. The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.

Title: Troubleshooting "MSVCP100.dll was not found" Error Message.
Content: Objective Learn how to resolve launch error with missing MSVCP100.dll This is caused by missing or outdated Visual C++ Redistributable which essential Windows component to running Marvelous Designer software. How to solve Visit Microsoft website, then download and install the latest Visual C++ Redistributable. The X64 architecture is recommended. Note In some cases, you may need to remove older versions of the Visual C++ Redistributables installed on your computer. The Visual C++ Redistributable is backward compatible with older versions, so we recommend installing only the most recent version.

Title: Line Tack on Avatar
Content: Objective Create lines on Garment and avatar and tack to each other by lines. (Ver. MD7) Location 3D window tool bar Line tack on Avatar tool Operation Select the tool according to the Location above. Mouse over to a garment from 3D window. Point follows mouse cursor. Double click on the garment where want to create start point of line / shape. Double click to complete the line / shape Double click on start point of line to create closed shape. Once a line is created on the garment, 3D garment will be transparent, can create line on the avatar directly. Create second line/ shape. Once all the two lines / shapes have been created, connection line for line / shape will be displayed. Click the simulation button. Two lines/ shapes tack to each other along the connection line. During the creation of the line, pressing the Shift key will display the front, back, side center line and guide line of last point. Press the Ctrl key to create curved line. When creating a line, can cancel it from the last point by pressing the Delete key on Keyboard. Press the Esc / Ctrl+Z to cancel the whole point.

Title: [Size Editor] Adjust Avatar Size (ver. 10)
Content: Objective Create an avatar with your own measurements. As Avatar Editor is powered by thousands of real body scan data, even measurements not assigned by users automatically adjust to the most realistic body shape. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Avatar Size Operation Load an Avatar (.avt). Only the avatars provided in ver. 10 V2 and above can be adjusted. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Avatar Size Measures appear on the Avatar. The editable measures appear in black, whereas the non-editable measures appear in grey. Refer to below graph and adjust the Avatar as needed. Option Description Select Avatar Select the Avatar to be edited. This option only appears when two or more Avatars are in the 3D window. Total Body Shape the overall body type with Avatar's height and chest width. In order to get realistic shapes for body parts without assignable measurements, use the Total Body option to create an overall shape and then insert measurements under the Details option. Height Assign Avatar's height. Note: * Use the drop-down menu on the right to select the unit of the Height. The default unit follows the program's unit. * Degree of Accuracy based on Height Measure Standard: HPS Height &gt Inseam &gt Total Height Total Height Insert the height measured from the ground to the head. Note: It is more accurate to assign height with either HPS Height or Inseam option as individual has different head length. The Total Height option is not recommended as it has the lowest accuracy. HPS Height Insert the height measured from the ground to the neck. Inseam Insert the height measured from the ground to the crotch. Width Select and insert desired value as the standard of the overall body width Details Configure Avatar's detailed measurements. Due to a technical reason, a small error may be generated even after inserting a specific measure. The error appears in parentheses next to each measurement and the real measurement can be checked with the measure appears on the Avatar. Edit the Avatar based on the measure appears on the Avatar as the numbers appear in the Avatar Editor only shows the measurements assigned by users. Note: * Use the drop-down menu on the right to select the unit of the Height. The default unit follows the program's unit. * Each measurement can be checked with the measure that appears on the Avatar. Basic Use the Basic option when only a small amount of body measurements are available. Unassigned body parts are automatically adjusted based on the real body scan data and the measurements inserted by the user. Advanced Use the Advanced option when available body measurements are abundant. When all measurements under the Advanced options are not available, please use the Basic option to create more realistic body as unassigned measurements are fixed with the default values pre-assigned to each option. Show All Measurements/ Show Editable Measurements By default, only editable measurements appear in the window. To view all measurements, click the Show All Measurements icon. * Use the Save button to save the adjusted measurements and use the Open button to reload. However, any measurements created with lower versions are not compatible.

Title: Rotate
Content: Objective Rotate Patterns and Internal Shapes/Lines based on various references. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Operation Rotate Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Select the Pattern or Internal Shapes/ Lines or Baselines to be rotated. The marquee box appears around the selected item. Click and drag the rotate point on top of the marquee box. The selected item rotates towards the mouse. Note: While clicking and dragging the Pattern, Internal Shapes/Lines, or Baselines, right click to access the Rotate window. Type in the desired angle, then click OK. The selected item rotates based on the entered value (ver3.2.0). Clockwise/Counterclockwise Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Click on the Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines to be rotated. Then, right click to access the pop-up menu. When the pop-up menu appears, select Clockwise (45º) or Clockwise (90º) or Counterclockwise (45º) or Counterclockwise (90º) The selected pattern rotates according to the chosen options. X/Y Axis Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Click on the Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines to be rotated. Then, right click to access the pop-up menu. When the pop-up menu appears, select X-Axis or Y-Axis. Select the line of a Pattern which should be rotated to the chosen axis. The selected Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines are rotated to X-Axis or Y-Axis on the basis of the selected line. Parallel To Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Click on the Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines to be rotated. Then, right click to access the pop-up menu. When the pop-up menu appears, select Parallel to... Select the line of any Patterns or Internal Lines/Shapes in the 2D window which the previously selected Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines are rotated to. This line acts as a fiducial line. The selected line turns red. Then, select the line of the rotating Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines that will rotate parallel to the fiducial line selected above. The Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines rotates parallel to the fiducial line.

Title: Merge Vertex by Proximity at Export
Content: Objective Merge vertices across patterns by proximity, without relying on sewing relationships, producing a single unified mesh which is "air-tight" across seams. This is especially useful for geometry which has been created using the Retopology Tools within Marvelous Designer. Once the new topology has been finalized, any sewing relationships are removed - so the previous sewing-relationship-based method of merging vertices at export would not be effective. Location Main Menu File Export OBJ Merge Vertex By Proximity Operation Load a project file with either traditional dynamic Marvelous Designer (Delaunay Triangulation) pattern meshes or non-dynamic pattern meshes created with the Retopology Tools in Marvelous Designer. Export the mesh through expanding the File dropdown-menu, selecting Export, then selecting OBJ. Set the file path for the OBJ and click Save. Export OBJ pop-up window appears. Check the option box for Merge Vertex by Proximity, above the option box for "Unified UV Coordinates". If the option is checked, the Weld and Thickness options are not available. Set the Merge Distance in listed scene units (mm by default). Preview the merged vertices in the (3D mesh) window.. Vertices which will be Merged can be highlighted in Red. Vertices which will not be Merged can be highlighted in Blue. Click OK

Title: Curved Side Geometry
Content: Objective Apply and adjust curvature on edges of Patterns for more natural and realistic look (ver2.2.0). Location 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Operation Firstly, change the 3D Garment rendering style to Thick Textured Surface in the 3D window. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Select a Pattern or Pattern line to express curved sided effect. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Enter a desired value at: Property Editor Selected Line Curved Side Geometry Curvature (%) The curvature is now being applied according to the entered value. Note: The maximum Curvature (%) value is 50 percent (%) of the fabric thickness. For instance, if the fabric thickness is being set at 1mm, the maximum Curvature (%) is 0.5mm.
